cash to be turned over? Could you reference a line number? I'm not seeing as soon as possible. Okay. So on line 13, as soon as possible was removed on that red line, on line 13, and I don't see that it's in there anywhere else. It's encompassed on line

10 through 12, that funds should be turned in no later than the end of the school day, which is then why on line 13, that as soon as possible was removed. Okay. Any more discuss-- Oh, Mr. Pepper. I know there's a big difference between should and shall, and I like the idea of shall because it's very specific. I do worry about those super weird random one-offs where someone might be ready to turn in the funds the next day, but the accounting-- So let me give you a concrete example because it's a little bit more convoluted than this. So very often I would run a school activity that collected cash,

and it ended very late at night after the bookkeeper was gone. I would go into the office and put that money into a safe, but I wouldn't necessarily have turned those funds in until the next day when I came in in the morning. Which is why I kind of like the should rather than the shall because it gives me just that little bit of leeway if someone said, "Well, you didn't actually turn those funds in, you put them safely in a safe." There's a little bit of leeway. I would be okay

with shall be turned in no later than the end of the school day or upon the conclusion of an activity. But I don't know how to caveat that. Does that make sense? For those weird random one-offs, which is why I think I'm leaning towards should just because of personal experience, but I see exactly where you're coming from. Yeah. I guess my question is, are there ever really instances where we're worried about cash not getting turned in in a timely manner?

We have a safe in every financial technician's office in this, as you stated before. Okay. So do we have issues with people not turning money in? So along those lines that because every school has a safe, I think that helps lessen the concern of the risk of money walking off before it could be deposited into the bank or brought over to the admin building. I'd also share that we don't have a large volume of cash and checks

also, so the risk is relatively low. So going a little further, I see the word safekeeping is in there, so I think that I'm actually okay with shall because I think it does encompass that kind of safe piece. Yeah. I don't want to make too big of an issue of it because I don't know enough about how this actual-- Especially now with digital transactions happening so often, I'm assuming checks and cash just are not something that we're dealing with in the volume we used to. So I don't want to make this an issue.

I just want to make sure that we're getting those funds as quickly as possible, put wherever they need to be put safely, and it's not an issue. And I appreciate the fact that we've cleaned this up a bunch, which I think is really helpful. Thanks. So with that, do we want to change it to shall or leave it as is? We can leave it as is for now. This is going to go to the full board. We can think about it and ruminate on whether there's a significant difference between should and shall.

We did receive one bid on this solicitation, and based on our review of the bid, the contract is recommended to be

awarded to Schmidt Baking Company, and the estimated amount is $298,200, which is in line with our anticipated spend for this item. And if approved, we would like to bring this back as either action or consent on the November 3rd Finance Committee meeting and on the school board consent agenda on November 10th, 2026. Thank you. Any discussion? Ms. Record. Just had a question. How often

do we only get a single bidder for something like this? Because I would assume- On school nutrition, almost every single contract that we put out is only one bid because of the size of our school system, the vast area that our school district covers, and the fact that we do regular weekly deliveries of our product and do not warehouse. It is very limited on the number of vendors that we get that respond to our solicitations for the school nutrition foods program. Interesting. Okay.

I'm surprised by that a bit, but I'm not doubting it, it's just I find it really interesting that there's just one bakery that's, I guess, big enough to service that. Is that... Big enough to service that. Also, the fresh bread requirements, the age of the product that is coming in, and other requirements within our school nutrition program. This is a issue that is larger districts across the state. Northern Virginia encounter this on a regular basis.

Also, keeping in mind they most likely also service Fairfax and Prince William. So because of the sheer volume, there is not a lot of vendors in our area that do this large of a product distribution. But historically, our school nutrition programs, when we put out contracts for any of those items, we generally get one bid. Interesting. Do we have the opportunity to work with smaller bakeries to be able to have-- Not that we want to manage multiple contracts- The- ... but I'm curious.

The only way we would be able to do that is to break the school district down into clusters. And when we did that, that would increase billing requirements and also the work we do behind the scenes to pay the invoices, as well as schedule and coordinate the deliveries. You would get into a situation where you would be working with multiple contracts for the same item.

Well, if there's no other discussion, I do find this conversation interesting because I was thinking of another bakery, and then you split half of Loudoun County schools and the other half. And we'll move on to 6.02, Support

Services Grant and Stream Restoration Floodplain, excuse me, Easements at Riverbend Middle School and Potomac Falls High School. This item is being presented by Mr. Pascarelli, Director of Construction. Thank you. Thank you. So this is an easement for the county, a floodplain easement at Riverbend in Potomac Falls. So as part of the county's mission to improve the quality of stormwater runoff,

the Department of General Services recently completed a stream restoration project in the streambed which lies between these two schools. The project involved removing invasive trees and underbrush, stabilizing the banks of the stream to prevent erosion, and new plantings of native species to create a natural habitat for native species. So as part of this process, the county performed what they call a floodplain study, resulting in a reduction of the area floodplain. So as a result,

they are seeking easements to define the areas of the floodplain as they are now, as well as to provide access so they can continue to maintain the stream and the floodplain. So, and I'm happy to answer any questions. Any discussion? Ms. Record. Oh, I have questions. Okay. So explain to me a little bit more about

the geography. Does this feed out into the Potomac, or is this some kind of tributary that's not- I don't know exactly where it feeds to, but I imagine it probably does. So this is a stream that goes between our two schools. It looks like Don may want to weigh in on that a little bit. So this stream does go between the two campuses and discharges into the Potomac River. Okay. All right. So I have lots of questions about the upstream, downstream of

this, right? So we're being asked to give the county access to manage this. Correct. Like really dumb this down for me so I can really wrap my head around it. So the work to stabilize the stream bed has already been done. So the invasives were already removed. The stream bed has been realigned, and they have replanted the entire

area. This easement and the floodplain easement gives them the ability to come back in and maintain it over time, so that they're not looking for us to try to do anything with it. This would be the county staff. They invested a lot of money stabilizing this, trying to reduce basically the flow of sediment and other things into the Potomac, clean up the Potomac, and they are asking for permission to basically set this aside so that they can maintain it in depth through

perpetually. Yeah. And I'm good for them maintaining that. I mean, for sure. I guess one of my questions is, is this part of the Broad Run stream? It is. Okay. So- What are the implications for the upstream, like the data center development runoff around the Broad Run stream upstream coming down here to this area towards the Potomac? Are we looking with this easement for

anything to get wide and expand? So this easement is only on our section of the property. And the stream bed, once again, the stream bed is already there, it's already established, and they are not widening the stream bed. They're not changing it from what's there right now. It has very little impact on what happens upstream,

with the exception of the way the stream bed has been designed in the floodplain area. It will facilitate, per se, better flow during floods, so you won't get the backup and the flooding up into the neighborhood that we have had in the past. It's not perfect. If in a heavy storm, it's still going to back up all the way up the floodplain. But this project was intended to focus just on the public land at the bottom end of the

stream, right as it's going into the river. Okay. And is there any cost to us for maintenance? There's no cost to us at all with this. The county covered all of the cost to do the work, and the county will cover all the cost to maintain it in the future. So they just want access. Giving them the easement and establishing the floodplain easement gives them access to the site. And obviously, it restricts our ability to do any buildings or anything growth in that area, but we couldn't build on the floodplain anyway. Right.

There's nothing we could do with that land. Our science classes have been going out. It's a pretty cool project. If you hadn't seen it, you can go down there and you walk around some and see where the restoration work has been done. Interesting. Okay. So it's an outdoor classroom space as well, sort of? I don't know if it's designated as an outdoor classroom space, but there is no reason that it could not be, and we can suggest that to Ms. Seipe and the sustainability team.

So when they did this work, it actually lessened the amount of area to which would be likely to

flood, as Mr. Treanor mentioned. And here's a diagram of the stream that goes between our two schools. Yeah, it's fascinating.
